title: Relay Loss in Ring Topology
description: This scenario explores relay loss dynamics within a ring communication topology. The disturbance creates coordination challenges that test the agents' ability to adapt, communicate effectively, and maintain freight flow under adverse conditions.
edge_cases_to_watch: Information Partitioning: Agent 'b' and 'd' can no longer communicate via agent 'a', forcing all multi-hop messages to traverse the longer path (b-c-d).
Congestion Cascades: The sudden shift in communication traffic from the direct path to the indirect path may delay critical coordination messages.
Deadlock via Silence: Agents may assume 'a' is incapacitated and stop assigning jobs to its location, causing freight stagnation at 'west' or 'north' depots.
Message Latency Jitter: Increased hop counts (from 1 to 3) causing timing mismatches in synchronized freight handoffs.
coordination_challenges: Path-finding in Communication: Agents must recalculate the shortest communicative path for multi-agent consensus.
Consensus Fragmentation: Reaching a global agreement on job priority becomes difficult when a subset of agents is isolated.
Resource Re-allocation: Re-assigning agent 'a's physical tasks to agents 'b' or 'd' without direct coordination with 'a'.
suggested_agent_strategies: Redundant Messaging: Send critical coordination packets to both neighbors to ensure packet arrival if one link is suspect.
Heartbeat Monitoring: Implement periodic 'alive' signals to distinguish between a broken link and a silent but active agent.
Adaptive Routing: If the 'a' link fails, immediately switch to a 'long-way-round' protocol for all inter-agent synchronization.
Proactive Buffer Management: Increase local inventory at depots near the muted agent to mitigate the risk of uncoordinated supply drops.
success_criteria: Agents adapt communication to topology constraints
Recovery from disruption within expected turns
Successful implementation of fallback communication protocols
